stories.delivered_paragraph: Trump Media & Technology Group has launched Truth API, a paid data feed promising Wall Street firms and institutional investors the fastest access to influential Truth Social posts. President Donald Trump’s account, with about 13 million followers, is the platform’s largest and potentially most market-moving, though the company has not said whether it is included. The service raises legal and ethical questions because Trump’s family remains the company’s majority shareholder while his public statements can move markets within seconds.

stories.delivered_paragraph: India is laying legal groundwork to let merchants potentially pay fees on some transactions through its Unified Payments Interface, ending the principle that accepting UPI payments is free. UPI processed a record 23.66 billion transactions worth ₹29.88 trillion, or about $313.4 billion, in July alone. The change could give banks and fintechs a more durable way to fund the fast-growing network, but would alter a zero-fee policy that helped drive its mass adoption since 2020.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Apple is seeking a preliminary injunction and expedited discovery in its trade-secrets case against OpenAI, alleging its technology may be used in an AI device or other products. In a new court filing, Apple said its investigation identified 11 additional former employees who may have witnessed or been involved in the alleged theft beyond the two employees initially accused. The request escalates a dispute that could expose more of OpenAI’s hardware-development plans and Apple’s confidential work.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A multistate lawsuit seeking to block the proposed $110 billion Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger has put CNN’s future at the center of the fight, according to Deadline. Paramount chief David Ellison has argued that concerns over CNN are the lawsuit’s real focus, while Ari Emanuel has publicly addressed fears that Larry Ellison could exert influence over both CNN and CBS. The case could determine whether the combined company proceeds and how its news operations are governed.

stories.delivered_paragraph: China’s electronics hub of Huaqiangbei lacks the parts needed to make exact copies of Apple’s newest phones, CNBC reported, a sign of changing access to the company’s supply chain. The report links that shortage to the so-called “Baby iPhone” and to a leak involving an Apple supplier, against a backdrop of Apple’s manufacturing expansion in India. Those shifts matter because they suggest China’s once-speedy ecosystem for copying and supplying consumer electronics is facing tighter constraints.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Authorities have made an arson arrest connected to the largest of several wildfires burning near Spokane, Washington, the BBC reported. Three fires in the area have forced about 60,000 people from their homes, underscoring the immediate scale of the emergency even as investigators pursue a possible criminal cause. The arrest may clarify how the biggest blaze began, while evacuation and firefighting efforts remain the priority for communities in the fire zone.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Crowds in Gaza City held a mass funeral for 112 Palestinians, mostly women and children, whose bodies were recently recovered from a residential block struck by Israel in November 2023. A two-week recovery operation pulled the remains of members of the Abu Sharia and Hassayna families from rubble in the Sabra neighborhood; the dead included 40 children and 38 women. The burial, described as Gaza’s largest such funeral, highlights how casualties from early fighting are still being recovered.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Cameroon’s 93-year-old President Paul Biya reshuffled senior military posts after being absent from public view for nearly two months, fueling concern over his prolonged stay abroad. He promoted five colonels to brigadier general and reappointed Raymond Jean Charles Beko’o Abondo to command the elite presidential guard, a post he has held since 2013. The moves echo earlier security reshuffles during periods of scrutiny and keep attention on political stability around one of Africa’s longest-serving leaders.

stories.delivered_paragraph: French authorities rescued more than 150 migrants after the engine of their boat caught fire as it attempted to cross the English Channel to the UK. The incident adds to the dangers facing people using overcrowded small boats on one of Europe’s busiest shipping routes. It is likely to intensify scrutiny of cross-Channel enforcement and rescue operations, even as authorities on both sides seek to deter the crossings.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Bowen Yang will make his Broadway acting debut as Mary Todd Lincoln in the Tony-winning comedy “Oh, Mary!” beginning September 15. The former “Saturday Night Live” cast member will take over from Meg Stalter for a limited 12-week run through December 6 at the Lyceum Theatre. Yang’s casting gives the long-running production another high-profile lead as it continues its Broadway run, West End engagement and planned North American tour.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Ed Sheeran co-wrote two of the top 10 songs on this week’s Billboard Global 200 despite not performing either one. Shakira and Burna Boy’s “Dai Dai,” the 2026 FIFA World Cup official song, held No. 1 for a fourth week with 56.8 million global streams, while KATSEYE’s “Animal” debuted at No. 10 on 29.8 million streams. The placements underline Sheeran’s continued commercial reach as a songwriter even while his own recordings have been absent from the global top 10.

stories.delivered_paragraph: U.S. manufacturing expanded at its fastest pace in more than four years in July, with the ISM index rising to 55.6, but factory executives also reported persistent price pressure and geopolitical uncertainty. The production measure jumped 6.3 points and manufacturing employment expanded for the first time in 33 months, while the prices index remained high at 71.1. The mix of stronger activity and stubborn inflation complicates the Federal Reserve’s path on interest rates.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Palantir shares jumped 27% after the software company reported second-quarter revenue of $1.94 billion, up 93% from a year earlier and above analysts’ $1.8 billion estimate. Commercial revenue surged 149% to $764 million as customers sought AI tools that let them keep control of their data, while government revenue rose 90% to $809 million. The results and raised outlook reinforce investor expectations that demand for enterprise AI is translating into unusually rapid sales growth.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Pfizer beat quarterly estimates and raised the low end of its full-year revenue guidance, citing strength in blood thinner Eliquis and other medicines. The update shows Pfizer is leaning more heavily on its non-Covid drug portfolio as the pandemic-era business continues to shrink.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Oil prices fell sharply after a Qatari official said the US and Iran could reach a short-term agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, MarketWatch reported. The route is vital to global energy shipments, so signs that traffic could normalize reduced the risk premium traders had placed on crude. Markets will now watch whether talks produce a workable deal, since any failure or renewed disruption could quickly reverse the move.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A MarketWatch analysis warns that delaying a Social Security claim until age 70 does more than increase a retiree’s initial monthly benefit: it also produces proportionally larger cost-of-living adjustments. The point adds a personal-finance wrinkle to the broader debate over Social Security’s funding shortfall. For retirees, the trade-off remains whether they can forgo earlier payments in exchange for a larger inflation-adjusted benefit later in life.
